````text
# #4039: Patch: in-game notifications that are kept until read: a feed in the inbox, toasts, the tab title and desktop notifications while JackiOh is open, in place of email
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

### What it does

The owners decided not to send player email through Resend for now (adding it later is a separate `human` issue, linked below). So JackiOh itself has to tell a player what happened, and keep telling them until they've seen it. Today it can't:

- **Nothing is kept.** The inbox (#3729, `apps/web/src/inbox/`) is worked out from lists the client already reads, with no server state (`store.ts`'s header). A lobby invite lives only in the tab's memory (`invites.ts`: "gone with the tab"). An invite sent while you're offline is lost.
- **Events that aren't "waiting on you" are never told at all:** a daily game ending (won, lost, drawn, on time), a friend accepting your request, a daily challenge you sent being accepted or declined.
- **Nothing reaches a tab in the background.** There's no title count outside `/daily` and the Duos board, and no desktop notification unless Web Push (VAPID) is set up.
- **The settings promise email that never comes.** "Email me when it's my move" (`apps/web/src/daily/NotificationSettings.tsx`) shows even though no email goes out without `PLAYER_RESEND_API_KEY`.

This adds a **notification feed kept on the server**, delivered live over the social socket, read in the inbox, and surfaced as a toast, in the tab's title, and as a desktop notification while JackiOh is open in any tab. Email and Web Push stay as they are, as extra channels when their keys are set (§9.13).

### What it should do

**1. A feed on the server** (`crates/server`, migration `0093` or the next free number):

- **The table:** `public.notifications`, one row per event for one account: id, `profile_id`, `kind`, the actor (a profile id, nullable), the subject (a daily match id, a lobby code, a replay id, as the kind needs), a small JSON payload for the words (a result, a format), `created_at` and `read_at`.
- **Access:** RLS on, no policy, no grant, as 0078's and 0092's tables: only the server's service role reads or writes it.
- **Keeping it small:** at most `NOTIFICATIONS_KEEP` rows per account (named constant in `crates/server/src/config.rs`, CLAUDE.md rule 9; say 100, newest kept), and the daily sweep drops rows older than `NOTIFICATIONS_KEEP_DAYS` (say 30).
- **Wiring:** register the migration in `crates/server/src/db/migrate.rs`, `crates/server/tests/store/migrations_pinned.rs` and both lists in `crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh`. Keep the in-memory fake (`db/fake.rs`) matching, with cases in `tests/store/contract.rs`.

The kinds, written by the code that already handles each event:

| Kind | When | To |
|---|---|---|
| `dailyMove` | a daily game begins waiting on you (the opponent moved, or the game started on your move) | the player now on move. One unread row per game: a newer move updates it, never stacks |
| `dailyEnded` | a daily game ends, including on time (R3727000) and by concession | both players, with the result each sees |
| `dailyChallenge` | a friend challenges you to a daily game | the challenged |
| `dailyAnswered` | your daily challenge is accepted or declined | the challenger |
| `friendRequest` | someone sends you a friend request | the asked |
| `friendAccepted` | your friend request is accepted | the asker |
| `lobbyInvite` | a friend invites you into their lobby (today's `lobbyInvite` frame, R3730005) | the invited. Stays listed until the lobby closes or starts |
| `replayShared` | a friend shares a replay with you | the friend |

A blocked account writes nothing to the one who blocked it, as the social reads already filter.

**2. Its API and live delivery:**

- `GET /api/notifications?before=<id>&limit=<n>`: newest first, paged, the caller's own only.
- `POST /api/notifications/read` `{upTo?}`: marks the caller's rows up to that id read, or all of them.
- The social socket (`crates/server/src/social/live.rs`) sends a `{type: "notification", ...}` frame with the new row to each of the account's tabs as it is written.
- The social read (`social/reads.rs`) gains `notificationsUnread` beside `dailyWaiting`.
- Rate-limit and auth as the other `/api/social` and `/api/daily` routes. Add the routes to `docs/v0.3.0/SURFACE.md` if that's where the boundary is listed.

**3. The web** (`apps/web`; CLAUDE.md rule 7: the client renders what the server sends and decides nothing):

- **Inbox panel:** below "Waiting on you", a **Recent** section lists the feed: one line each ("Ana accepted your friend request", "Your daily game with Bo ended: you won on time"), how long ago, and a link to its screen. Unread rows carry a dot. Opening the panel marks what it shows read. It pages back on scroll or with a "Show older" button.
- **The bell's badge:** stays the count of what needs you, per the brief's "badges only for what needs you" (#3728's `docs/polish/10-menus.md`). Unread Recent rows add only a small dot to the bell.
- **Toasts:** a notification that arrives while the app is open shows a toast, at most one at a time in the existing toast style. It shows the line and an "Open" action. Kinds that already have a toast (`ChallengeToast.tsx`, `LobbyInviteToast.tsx`) keep theirs and show no second one. A toast never covers the game board's controls during a live match: hold it until the match ends, or show it in the shell's status slot only.
- **Tab title:** while the tab is hidden, the title starts with the bell's count, e.g. "(2) JackiOh". The board routes that already set their own title (`DailyRoute.tsx`, `DuosRoute.tsx`) keep theirs.
- **Desktop notifications while JackiOh is open:** the Notifications settings section (`NotificationSettings.tsx`, also `/account`'s section) gains "Show notifications on this computer while JackiOh is open". It asks the browser's Notification permission and, while the tab is hidden, shows one with the browser's Notification API for `dailyMove`, `dailyChallenge`, `lobbyInvite` and `friendRequest` arrivals. This needs no push service and no VAPID keys. The existing Web Push toggle stays for when the app is closed.
- **Email toggle:** shown only when the server can send email. `GET /api/daily/settings` gains `emailAvailable` (the player mailer is configured, i.e. `PLAYER_RESEND_API_KEY` is set). When it's false, the section says, in the game's voice, that JackiOh tells you here, in the bell and on this device, instead of offering a toggle that does nothing.
- **Strings:** new strings go through `t()`, with their `zh-CN.json` entries as the project does for every string.

**4. Docs and spec:**

- §9.13's Notifications bullet names the in-game feed as the channel that is always on, with email and push as extras when their keys are set. Add a short spec section for the feed (its kinds, how long it's kept, the `notification` frame) where the social reads are specified.
- Any decision the spec doesn't make gets a ruling in this issue's block, with its proving test (CLAUDE.md rule 3).
- `crates/server/README.md` and `apps/web/README.md` say what's new.

### Tests (each fails without the change)

- **Server API**, in `crates/server/tests/api/`:
  - Each kind in the table is written when its event happens, to the right account, and no others.
  - `dailyMove` updates instead of stacking.
  - The cap and the age purge hold.
  - `read` marks only the caller's rows.
  - The `notification` frame reaches each of the account's open sockets.
  - A blocked account writes nothing.
- **Store:** `tests/store/contract.rs` covers memory and Postgres for insert, the per-game update, the page, `read` and the purge. `tests/sql/` covers RLS: `anon` and `authenticated` can't read or write the table.
- **Web unit:**
  - The Recent section renders and pages.
  - Opening the panel calls `read`.
  - A `notification` frame shows one toast, and none for kinds that have their own.
  - The title count shows only while the tab is hidden.
  - The desktop toggle asks permission and notifies only while hidden.
  - The email toggle is hidden when `emailAvailable` is false.
- **E2E:** a spec where the opponent's daily move, sent over HTTP as spec 52 does, shows the mover's opponent a toast and a Recent row without a reload, in a built client against the E2E server.

### Not in scope

- Email of any kind: see the linked `human` issue.
- Sounds.
- Notifications for things the inbox already handles live within minutes (a live challenge's own toast stays as it is).

### Screenshots

The bot can't attach them. A session will take the inbox with Recent, a toast and the Notifications section at the seven device sizes after it merges.

### Part of

Follows the tracker #3726 (daily games, the inbox #3729). The owners decided against Resend for now, 2026-11-16.

## Goal

A feed kept on the server (migration 0093, `public.notifications`). Each of the eight events writes to it where that event is already handled. It is read by `GET /api/notifications` and `POST /api/notifications/read`, pushed as a `notification` frame on `/ws/social`, and counted as `notificationsUnread` in the social read. Each profile keeps at most `NOTIFICATIONS_KEEP` rows, and rows older than `NOTIFICATIONS_KEEP_DAYS` are purged.

The web shows the feed as the inbox's Recent section, a dot on the bell, one toast at a time, a `(n)` tab title while the tab is hidden, and desktop notifications. ## Steps

**Server**

1. **`0093_notifications.sql`.** Write its header in 0092's style.
   - The table:
     ```sql
     create table if not exists public.notifications (
       id bigint generated always as identity primary key,
       profile_id uuid not null references public.profiles(id) on delete cascade,
       kind text not null constraint notifications_kind_check check (kind in ('dailyMove','dailyEnded','dailyChallenge','dailyAnswered','friendRequest','friendAccepted','lobbyInvite','replayShared')),
       actor_id uuid references public.profiles(id) on delete cascade,
       subject text,
       payload jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb,
       created_at bigint not null,
       read_at bigint
     )
     ```
   - Three indexes: `(profile_id, id desc)`, `(actor_id)` (CHECK 19 wants every foreign key indexed) and `(created_at)`.
   - A table comment, RLS on, `revoke all … from public, anon, authenticated`, and the closing summary of what each role may do.
   - Add the file to `MIGRATIONS`.

2. **`config.rs`.** After `// ---- end Social ----`, add `NOTIFICATIONS_KEEP: i64 = 100`, `NOTIFICATIONS_KEEP_DAYS: i64 = 30`, `NOTIFICATIONS_PAGE: i64 = 20` and `NOTIFICATIONS_PAGE_MAX: i64 = 50`. Give each a `/// R4039000: …` comment. None of them is exported to the client.

3. **`notifications/store.rs`.** Copy `lobby/store.rs`'s shape: its own dispatch macro, a `mod pg` and a `mod fake`.
   - Types:
     - `NotificationRow { id: i64, profile_id, kind: String, actor_id: Option<String>, subject: Option<String>, payload: Value, created_at: i64, read_at: Option<i64> }`.
     - `NewNotification`: the same fields without `id` and `read_at`.
     - Both derive `Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq`, camelCase.
     - `NotificationTables { rows, next_id: i64 }`, deriving `Default`.
   - `Tx` methods:
     - `notifications_add(&NewNotification, keep: i64) -> NotificationRow`, in three statements:
       1. Delete the profile's unread row of the same kind whose `actor_id` and `subject` match (`is not distinct from`).
       2. Insert the new row with `returning`.
       3. Delete the profile's rows outside its newest `keep` by id.
     - `notifications_page(profile_id, before: Option<i64>, limit: i64)`: rows with `id < before`, id descending.
     - `notifications_unread(profile_id) -> i64`.
     - `notifications_mark_read(profile_id, up_to: Option<i64>, at: i64) -> u64`: marks unread rows with `id <= up_to`, or all of them for `None`.
     - `notifications_delete(profile_id, ids: &[i64]) -> u64`.
     - `notifications_purge(before: i64) -> u64`: deletes rows with `created_at < before`.
   - pg:
     - Call `run_as(t, None)` and use `::uuid` and `::jsonb` casts.
     - Bind the payload with `json(&payload)?`. Read it with `row.try_get::<Value, _>("payload")?`, as `lobby_of` does (`json_col` is private to `pg.rs`).
     - Read ids with `uuid_text` and `uuid_text_or_null`.
     - A `profile_id` that is not a uuid reads as empty or 0, checked with `is_uuid` as `push_subs_of` does.
   - fake: each method calls `crate::db::fake::call(f, "notifications.add")` (and so on), and ids come from `next_id += 1`.
   - `pub fn remove_notification_rows(tables, profile_id)` drops every row naming that profile as `profile_id` or as `actor_id`.

4. **`fake.rs`.** `FakeTables` gains `pub notifications: crate::notifications::store::NotificationTables`. `remove_profile_rows` calls `remove_notification_rows` after its daily line.

5. **`notifications/mod.rs`.**
   - `enum Kind` with the eight variants; `as_str()` spells them as the SQL check does.
   - `pub struct Notice { to, kind, actor: Option<String>, subject: Option<String>, payload: Value }`.
   - `pub async fn notify(app: &App, notices: Vec<Notice>)`:
     1. With no notices, return at once.
     2. Open one transaction. Skip a notice whose actor is `to`, or where `tx.blocks_between(actor, to)` is true.
     3. Write each of the others with `notifications_add(…, NOTIFICATIONS_KEEP)`, stamped `now_ms()`.
     4. Read the actors through `social::profiles_by_id`, then commit.
     5. For each written row, call `live::send_notification(app, &row.profile_id, &notification_json(&row, actor))`. Then call `push_social` for the recipients.
     6. Log any error as `tracing::warn!(event = "notifications.write_failed", …)` and never return it.
     - Callers call `notify` after their own commit, on the success path only.
   - `notification_json(row, actor: Option<&PlayerRef>)` answers `{id, kind, actor: {profileId, username} | null, subject, payload, createdAt, read}`.
   - `list` (`GET /api/notifications`):
     - Read `before` (a positive integer) and `limit` (1 to `NOTIFICATIONS_PAGE_MAX`, default `NOTIFICATIONS_PAGE`) from `req.query`. Anything else is `bad_request`.
     - Read `limit + 1` rows and keep `limit`. `nextBefore` is the last kept id when more rows exist, else null.
     - For each `lobbyInvite` row, call `lobbies_get(subject)`. If the lobby is gone, started, or has `expires_at <= now`, drop the row from the answer and delete it with `notifications_delete`.
     - Answer `200 {notifications, nextBefore, unread}`.
   - `mark_read` (`POST /api/notifications/read`):
     - `upTo` may be absent, null or a positive integer; anything else is 400.
     - Mark at `now_ms()` and commit, then call `push_social(app, &[&me])`.
     - Answer `200 {unread}`.

6. **`app.rs`.** In `ROUTES`, after `/api/social`, add:
   - `("GET", "/api/notifications", AuthLevel::Active, h!(crate::notifications::list))`
   - `("POST", "/api/notifications/read", AuthLevel::Active, h!(crate::notifications::mark_read))`

   R109's limiter covers them like every other Active route.

7. **`live.rs` and `reads.rs`.**
   - In `live.rs`, add `pub fn send_notification(app: &App, to: &str, notification: &Value)`. It sends `{"type": "notification", "notification": …}` through `send_to`. The file header now lists six frames.
   - In `reads.rs`, add `"notificationsUnread": tx.notifications_unread(me).await?` inside its existing transaction.

8. **`games.rs`, `apply`.**
   - Right after `tx.commit()`, capture `let before = loaded.daily.clock.clone();` and `let sender = loaded.account_at(row.action.player_id).to_string();`.
   - After the `record` call, add `crate::notifications::notify(app, feed_notices(loaded, &before, &sender)).await;`.
   - Add a private `fn feed_notices(loaded: &Loaded, before: &DailyClock, sender: &str) -> Vec<Notice>`. For every notice the actor is the other player and the subject is the match id.
     - **The game ended:** `loaded.daily.board.result` is set and is not `Voided`. Send `dailyEnded` to both players. The payload is `{outcome, reason}`, computed as `summary_json` computes them (through `seat_now`).
     - **Otherwise:** send `dailyMove` (payload `{}`) for each hold in `loaded.daily.clock.holds` where both hold:
       - `before.hold_of(hold.player).is_none_or(|old| old.since != hold.since)`;
       - `loaded.account_at(hold.player) != sender`.
   - A loss on time is covered too, because `settle` goes through `apply`.

9. **`invites.rs`.** Each notice comes after the handler's commit, with actor `me`:
   - `challenge`: `dailyChallenge` to `friend_id`, subject `row.id`, payload `{mode, perMoveDays}`.
   - `accept`: `dailyAnswered` to `invite.from_profile`, subject `invite.id`, payload `{answer: "accepted", matchId}`.
   - `seek`, when it pairs: `dailyMove` to `other.from_profile`, subject the match id.
   - `close`, only `if matches!(state, DailyInviteState::Declined)`: `dailyAnswered` with payload `{answer: "declined"}`.

10. **`notify.rs`.**
    - `settings_json` adds `"emailAvailable": app.daily.mailer.is_some()`.
    - `sweep`'s first transaction runs `notifications_purge(now - NOTIFICATIONS_KEEP_DAYS * MS_PER_DAY)` and logs `notifications.purged` when it deleted any. `Swept` stays as it is.

11. **Friends, shares and lobbies.** Payload `{}` unless named, actor `me`:
    - `post_request`, mutual path: `friendAccepted` to `target.id`, subject `theirs.id`.
    - `post_request`, normal path: `friendRequest` to `target.id`, subject `request.id`.
    - `accept_request`: `friendAccepted` to `sender_id`, subject `request_id`.
    - `share_replay`: `replayShared` to `friend_id`, subject `match_id`.
    - `lobby::invite`, after `send_lobby_invite`: `lobbyInvite` to `friend_id`, subject `lobby.code`, payload `{format}`.

**Web** (CLAUDE.md rule 7: the client renders what the server sends)

12. **`net/notifications.ts`.**
    - Types: `FeedKind`, `FeedNotification` (step 5's JSON shape) and `NotificationsPage`.
    - `isFeedNotification(value: unknown)`, a hand-written guard like `isChallenge`.
    - `getNotifications(before?: number)` keeps only rows that pass the guard.
    - `markNotificationsRead(upTo?: number)`.
    - Both go through a local `feed<T>` copied from `social<T>` in `net/social.ts`.

13. **The social read and socket.**
    - `SocialRead` gains `notificationsUnread?: number`.
    - `socialSocket.ts`: the `social` case keeps `notificationsUnread` when it is a number. `SocialPush` gains `{ kind: "notification"; notification: FeedNotification }`.
    - `socialPoll.ts`:
      - `SocialReads` gains `notificationsUnread`: 0 in `EMPTY` and in the refused read, and read in `applySocial` through `dailyWaitingOf`.
      - Add a listener set and the `onPush` case.
      - Add `export function onNotificationPush(listener): () => void`, written like `onLobbyInvitePush`.

14. **`inbox/feed.ts`.** A module store like `invites.ts`, holding `{ rows, nextBefore, error }`.
    - `openFeed()` reads the first page. If any row is unread it calls `markNotificationsRead(rows[0].id)`, then `reloadSocial()`.
    - `loadOlderFeed()` appends the page before `nextBefore`.
    - `resetFeedForTests()`.
    - `feedLine(row)`, every string through `t()`. With no actor, the name is `t("Someone")`.

      | Kind | Line |
      |---|---|
      | dailyMove | "Your move against {name}" |
      | dailyEnded | "Your daily game with {name} ended: you won", "…: you won on time" (reason `disconnect`), "…: you lost", "…: you lost on time", "…: it was a draw" |
      | dailyChallenge | "{name} challenged you to a daily game" |
      | dailyAnswered | "{name} accepted your daily challenge", "{name} declined your daily challenge" |
      | friendRequest | "{name} sent you a friend request" |

## Risks

- **Exact-body asserts break.** `social.rs` and `social_live.rs:141` compare the whole social body. Never hardcode the unread count.
- **A handler must never fail because of the feed.** `notify` runs after the commit and only logs its errors.
- **Hidden information.** A page reads only the caller's own rows, and actors are `PlayerRef`s.
- **Seat swaps (R677).** Use `loaded.account_at` after the action, and take `before` from the clock as it was before the action.
- **Replay.** Nothing enters `GameState` or the log, so replay, fuzz and golden are unaffected.
````

## Goal

A feed kept on the server (migration 0093, `public.notifications`). Each of the eight events writes to it where that event is already handled. It is read by `GET /api/notifications` and `POST /api/notifications/read`, pushed as a `notification` frame on `/ws/social`, and counted as `notificationsUnread` in the social read. Each profile keeps at most `NOTIFICATIONS_KEEP` rows, and rows older than `NOTIFICATIONS_KEEP_DAYS` are purged.

The web shows the feed as the inbox's Recent section, a dot on the bell, one toast at a time, a `(n)` tab title while the tab is hidden, and desktop notifications. It hides the email toggle when `emailAvailable` is false. §9.4, §9.13, rulings R4039000 (server) and R4039001 (client) and the READMEs record all of this.
